metadata.case_name: CHAN WAI KEUNG v. LI YAU HING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: resumed work as a plasterer (light duties only for some nine to ten months); thereafter unemployed and sought casual work and security guard posts (unsuccessful)

injuries.description: a fracture of the right mid-tibia.
source: a fracture of the right mid-tibia.

manifestations.description: continuous attacks of right heel pain aggravated by prolonged walking and standing for over an hour
could not climb up and down bamboo scaffolds
could not squat and had to adjust by kneeling on right knee causing right knee pain
right heel pain when lifting heavy object and only managed to lift objects of less than 20 catties
muscle cramp of right lower limb at night about once a week
less steady on the right side for single leg standing
"L" shape scar over the lateral aspect of the right heel at 4 cm x 7 cm well healed and pigmented
tenderness along scar, medial aspect and plantar
50% decrease in sensation to touch over lateral aspect of right ankle
muscle atrophy of right calf at 1 cm comparing with 36.6 cm on the left calf
tenderness over lateral right calf (physiotherapy report)
range of right ankle movement full (physiotherapy report)

treatments_received: internal fixation of the fracture (operation on 16 October 2009)
occupational physiotherapy (14 sessions from 12 February to 4 June 2010)
regular outpatient follow-ups at Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology

losses.description: Residual pain especially when walking on uneven grounds, climbing up and down frequently, lifting and carrying heavy objects, squatting, prolonged walking and prolonged standing
Cannot resume working as a plasterer; reduced working efficiency and capacity and disadvantage in the labour market
"L" shape scar over the lateral aspect of the right heel at 4 cm x 7 cm well healed and pigmented
